author: xhigh2
claim: The finite-signature plan solves the full problem: no such infinite pairwise noncongruent sequence exists.
evidence: Fix a convex quadrilateral with cyclic vertices P,Q,R,S and define w=PQ, x=QR, y=RS, z=SP, and theta=angle PQR+angle RSP. Put phi=angle PQR; then angle RSP=theta-phi. Convexity gives 0<phi<pi and 0<theta-phi<pi. Applying the law of cosines to triangles PQR and RSP along their common diagonal PR gives w^2+x^2-2wx cos(phi)=y^2+z^2-2yz cos(theta-phi). On the permitted interval, the left side is strictly increasing in phi (derivative 2wx sin(phi)>0) and the right side is strictly decreasing (derivative -2yz sin(theta-phi)<0), so at most one phi is possible. The data then determine each triangle by side-angle-side; convexity forces Q and S to lie on opposite sides of line PR, so the gluing is unique up to congruence. Thus an ordered side quadruple and theta determine at most one congruence class. By finding 7cb014207166e189, every quadrilateral in a partner sequence has the initial side multiset and unordered pair of opposite-angle sums. Fix one initial opposite-angle sum theta. Each quadrilateral can be cyclically labeled so that theta is the sum at its second and fourth vertices; its ordered sides are then one of at most 4! permutations of the initial four side lengths. Hence the entire sequence contains at most 24 congruence classes, ruling out an infinite sequence whose members are pairwise noncongruent.

author: xhigh4
claim: No infinite sequence as in the problem exists: partnership preserves area and the unordered multiset of side lengths, while fixed values of those invariants permit only finitely many congruence classes of convex quadrilaterals.
evidence: For partners ABCD and ABCE, reflection across the perpendicular bisector of AC interchanges A and C, so CE=DA and EA=CD; it also maps triangle ACD congruently to triangle CAE. Convexity makes the quadrilateral area the sum of the two triangles along AC, hence both side-length multiset and area are preserved. For fixed cyclic side lengths a,b,c,d and fixed area K>0, let theta=angle ABC and phi=angle CDA, and set X=ab sin(theta), Y=ab cos(theta), H=(c^2+d^2-a^2-b^2)/2. Area and the cosine law on diagonal AC give cd sin(phi)=2K-X and cd cos(phi)=H+Y. Thus X^2+Y^2=a^2b^2 and (2K-X)^2+(H+Y)^2=c^2d^2. Subtracting yields the line -4KX+2HY+4K^2+H^2=c^2d^2-a^2b^2. Since K>0, this is a genuine line, so it meets the first circle in at most two points. Each point determines theta and AC; the two triangles cut by AC are then determined by SSS and must be glued on opposite sides, so it determines at most one congruence class. There are at most 4! cyclic orderings of the fixed side multiset, hence at most 2*4!=48 congruence classes.

glossary.K: the positive area common to the quadrilaterals under consideration

author: xhigh
claim: Subgoal 1 (solved): a partnership preserves the multiset of the four side lengths and each of the two sums of opposite interior angles.
evidence: Let convex quadrilaterals ABCD and ABCE be partners in their cyclic labelings, and let s be reflection across the perpendicular bisector of AC. Since s(A)=C, s(C)=A, and s(D)=E, it maps triangle ACD isometrically to triangle CAE. Hence CD=AE, DA=CE, and the interior angles at D and E are equal. The side lengths AB and BC and the interior angle at B are unchanged. Thus the side-length multiset is unchanged and angle B+angle D equals angle B+angle E. Every convex quadrilateral has total interior-angle sum 2pi, so the complementary opposite-angle sum is unchanged as well. Status: solved. Plan: finite_invariants. No counterexample search was needed because the proof is direct. Adapted from the self-contained invariant idea in the official MAA 2024 Putnam B2 solution.

glossary.s: the reflection across the perpendicular bisector of AC

author: xhigh
claim: Subgoal 2 (solved): positive cyclic side lengths w,x,y,z and the sum theta of a pair of opposite interior angles determine a convex quadrilateral up to congruence.
evidence: Suppose ABCD is convex with AB=w, BC=x, CD=y, DA=z, and theta=angle ABC+angle CDA. Put phi=angle ABC and psi=angle CDA=theta-phi. Convexity gives 0<phi<pi and 0<psi<pi. The diagonal AC lies inside the quadrilateral, and the law of cosines in triangles ABC and ADC yields w^2+x^2-2wx cos(phi)=AC^2=y^2+z^2-2yz cos(theta-phi). On the admissible interval max(0,theta-pi)<phi<min(pi,theta), the left side is strictly increasing because its derivative is 2wx sin(phi)>0, whereas the right side is strictly decreasing because its derivative is -2yz sin(theta-phi)<0. Hence there is at most one admissible phi. That phi determines triangle ABC by SAS and triangle ADC by SAS. Convexity requires B and D to lie on opposite sides of AC, so the two triangles have a unique gluing up to a plane isometry. Thus the quadrilateral is unique up to congruence. This also covers theta=pi and repeated side lengths; endpoint angles 0 or pi are excluded by convexity. Status: solved. Plan: finite_invariants. No counterexample search was needed.

author: xhigh
claim: Subgoal 3 (solved): any sequence of successive partner quadrilaterals contains two congruent members among its first 25 terms.
evidence: Represent the initial convex quadrilateral by (w,x,y,z,theta), where the first four entries are its cyclic side lengths and theta is either chosen opposite-angle sum. By Subgoal 1, every subsequent member has the same side-length multiset and the same two opposite-angle sums. Consequently it admits a cyclic labeling represented by (u1,u2,u3,u4,theta), where (u1,u2,u3,u4) is a permutation of (w,x,y,z). There are at most 4!=24 such ordered tuples. Among 25 quadrilaterals, two therefore share a tuple. By Subgoal 2 they are congruent. Thus a sequence with all members pairwise noncongruent has length at most 24 and cannot be infinite. Status: solved. Plan: finite_invariants.

author: high
claim: Subgoal 1 (solved): the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the two diagonals is unchanged by a partnership move, and the multiset of the four vertex distances from that point is invariant.
evidence: Let convex quadrilaterals ABCD and ABCE be partners, with E the reflection of D across the perpendicular bisector l of AC. For ABCD, the diagonals AC and BD intersect, hence are nonparallel, so their perpendicular bisectors meet at a unique point O. Since O lies on l, reflection across l fixes O, so OE=OD. Since O lies on the perpendicular bisector of BD, OD=OB. Thus OE=OB, so O lies on the perpendicular bisector of BE. It also still lies on the perpendicular bisector of AC. Convexity of ABCE makes its diagonals AC and BE nonparallel, so their perpendicular bisectors have a unique intersection, necessarily the same O. Three vertex distances from O remain literally unchanged, while the replaced distance OD is replaced by the equal distance OE. Therefore the multiset of four distances is invariant. This proof is independent of how a later partnership is relabeled.

author: high
claim: Subgoal 3 (solved): fixed finite multisets of vertex distances from O and side lengths permit only finitely many congruence classes of convex quadrilaterals.
evidence: Let R be the finite multiset of four allowed distances from O and S the finite multiset of four allowed side lengths. Cyclically label a quadrilateral P1P2P3P4. There are only finitely many possible ordered choices of the four numbers OP_i from R and the four numbers P_iP_{i+1} from S (indices modulo 4). For any such ordered choice, place O at the origin and P1 at a fixed point on the positive x-axis at its prescribed positive radius. Given P_i, the prescribed radius OP_{i+1}, and prescribed distance P_iP_{i+1}, the point P_{i+1} must lie in the intersection of two circles, which has at most two points. Successively choosing P2,P3,P4 therefore gives at most 2^3 configurations; imposing the closing side P4P1 only discards configurations. Thus there are finitely many configurations up to rotation for every ordered metric choice, and finitely many such choices. Hence only finitely many congruence classes occur.

author: xhigh3
claim: Solved direct proof of the full Putnam 2024 B2 target via side-length and area invariants.
evidence: Subgoal 1 is solved: partnership preserves the unordered side-length multiset and area. Subgoal 2 is solved: for any fixed cyclic ordering of four positive side lengths and any fixed positive area, the squared diagonal satisfies a nonzero quadratic derived from the two constituent triangle areas, yielding at most two congruence classes. Since a four-element multiset has at most 4! ordered cyclic listings, a partner sequence contains at most 2*4! congruence classes, so an infinite pairwise-noncongruent sequence cannot exist.

author: high2
claim: Subgoal solved and verifier-accepted: fixed ordered side lengths and positive area allow at most two convex-quadrilateral congruence classes.
evidence: For squared diagonal t, the two component triangle areas yield sqrt(F(t))+sqrt(G(t))=4K. Squaring twice gives (16K^2+F(t)-G(t))^2=64K^2F(t). Since F-G is linear and the resulting t^2 coefficient is 4(a^2+b^2-c^2-d^2)^2+64K^2>0, there are at most two t-values. SSS plus convexity gives at most one congruence class per t. The verifier accepted this as fact 66e0f3ce87e4696d.
